coordinates.note: No official KamLAND page or paper consulted (checked 2026-09-17) states numeric coordinates. This is the Wikipedia coordinate, so it is shown as a campus-grade, approximate point and not as an underground-laboratory position. KamLAND occupies the original Kamiokande cavity in the Kamioka mine, the same general underground complex as the Kamioka Observatory's primary site at Mozumi (Super-Kamiokande).

name: KamLAND cavity, Kamioka mine
notes: Wikipedia states an overburden of '105 m.w.e.' for KamLAND. This is inconsistent with the ~2700 m.w.e. given for the same Kamioka/Mozumi mine by the Kamioka Observatory record (from the ICRR facility page and the Super-Kamiokande NIM paper), and is very likely a Wikipedia error or a different overburden metric. It is deliberately not recorded here, so depth and water-equivalent depth are left empty rather than citing an implausible figure.

summary.plain: The cavern in the Kamioka mine in Japan, originally dug for the first Kamiokande detector, that now holds the KamLAND reactor-antineutrino detector.
summary.technical: Underground cavity within the Kamioka mine (facility:kamioka-observatory), reusing the original Kamiokande excavation, housing the KamLAND liquid-scintillator antineutrino detector.
